questions.question: How much of each registered transfer observable is attributable to drift?
questions.falsifier: The registered drift contribution or forward persistence vanishes, reverses, or falls inside declared numerical or measurement uncertainty under matched controls.

questions.question: Which geometry variables gate transfer magnitude, sign, direction, timing, and work?
questions.falsifier: A registered sign-reversing or null geometry intervention does not change the proposed pathway beyond uncertainty, or the effect fails in an independent engine.

questions.question: Which timing patterns and failure modes matter, including casting, insufficient early proximal acceleration, and segment release timing?
questions.falsifier: The proposed timing mechanism loses its benefit under matched work/state, reverses under a plausible event definition, or is dominated by load or orientation cost.

questions.question: Does passive or drift-mediated transfer reduce required timing precision?
questions.falsifier: The drift-mediated policy has an equal or smaller viable region, worse lower-tail outcome, or greater delay/phase sensitivity after force and effort costs are matched.

questions.question: Are any strategies self-correcting, noise-rejecting, or more robust?
questions.falsifier: Perturbations do not decay, recovery is not more probable than the comparator, or any benefit requires an unregistered force/load increase.

questions.question: Must proximal velocity be maximized to maximize transfer?
questions.falsifier: The proposed monotonic benefit shows a plateau, interior optimum, reversal, adverse load, or dependence on the matching rule.

questions.question: When is slack beneficial, harmful, or required?
required_controls: one slack class at a time
questions.falsifier: A proposed slack benefit disappears when slack classes are separated, violates passivity/energy closure, or is non-identifiable from the available measurements.
